column3: NASB follows the critical text; it renders “comfort” as “consolation” and “affections and compassions” in the singular.
NASB renders “fulfill” as “make … complete,” “united in soul” as “united in spirit,” and “minding the same thing” as “intent on one purpose.”
NASB follows the critical text; “self-interest” is rendered “selfishness,” and “vain conceit” is “empty conceit.” It adds “let each of you.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “merely” and “personal interests.”
NASB follows the critical text without “for”; “be thinking” is rendered “Have this attitude.”
NASB adds “although” and renders “considered” as “regard.”
NASB ends the verse at “likeness of men,” moving “being found in appearance as a man” into v. 8; “servant” is rendered “bond-servant.”
NASB begins with “being found in appearance as a man,” moved from v. 7; “unto death” is rendered “to the point of death.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the name”); “granted” is rendered “bestowed.”
NASB puts the allusion in capitals and adds “of those who are.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “Therefore” as “So then.”
NASB follows the critical text; “according to” is rendered “for.”
NASB renders “murmurings and disputings” as “grumbling or disputing.”
NASB follows the critical text (“blameless”); it renders “may be” as “prove yourselves to be” and “shine” as “appear.”
NASB renders “holding forth” as “holding fast” and “unto a boast to me” as “I may have cause to glory.”
NASB adds “as a drink offering” and renders “rejoice with” as “share my joy with.”
NASB adds “I urge you” and renders “rejoice with me” as “share your joy with me.”
NASB renders “the things concerning you” as “your condition.”
NASB adds “else” and renders “like-minded” as “of kindred spirit.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Christ Jesus”).
NASB restructures the verse.
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB renders “I have been persuaded” as “I trust.”
NASB renders “I esteemed” as “I thought.”
NASB has no “to see,” following the critical text; “deeply distressed” is rendered “distressed.”
NASB renders “nearly unto death” as “to the point of death.”
NASB renders “more speedily” as “more eagerly” and adds “about you.”
NASB renders “such” as “men like him” and “in honor” as “in high regard.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “disregarded his life” as “risking his life.”
